options: Stack overflow — the calls never stop
javascript:10.explain: Every call uses stack memory until it runs out.

javascript:10.prompt: Which data structure stores the pending recursive calls?
javascript:10.explain: Each call pushes a stack frame.

int is 32-bit (−2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647). Going past the limit wraps around silently (overflow). Use long (suffix L) for bigger values. → 2147483647
Math.pow, sqrt, ceil, floor and hypot return DOUBLE (printed with .0); Math.round returns long; Math.max/min keep the wider type; floorDiv/floorMod round toward −∞. → -7.0

Bitwise operators work on binary: 3 = 11, 1 = 1. & AND, | OR, ^ XOR, << left shift, >> signed right shift, >>> unsigned right shift, ~ NOT (−n − 1). → false

options: Stack overflow — the calls never stop

java:10.prompt: Which data structure stores the pending recursive calls?

The recursive call is the first statement
java:10.explain: Nothing is left to do after the call returns.

options: The recursive call happens before the other work in the function
The call is the last operation

Recursion on tree data structures only
A call passed as an argument
A function without a base case

options: Function A calls B and B calls A
A function calls a library function
java:10.explain: The cycle goes through another function.

options: A recursive call is used as the argument of another recursive call
A recursive function defined inside another
A function calls itself within its own body

options: Each call makes at most one recursive call

java:10.explain: Store results in a cache and reuse them.

java:10.prompt: How many calls does fact(5) make including the first call (base case n <= 1)?
java:10.explain: fact(5) → fact(4) → fact(3) → fact(2) → fact(1).

options: Split the problem into halves, solve each recursively, and combine

cpp:8.explain: n rows going up and n − 1 rows coming down.

cpp:8.prompt: What does the OUTER loop usually control in a pattern program?

cpp:10.explain: A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller input.

cpp:10.prompt: What is the base case in recursion?
options: The condition that stops the recursion
The first call to the function
cpp:10.explain: Without a base case recursion never ends.

cpp:10.prompt: What happens if a recursive function has no base case?
options: Stack overflow — the calls never stop
cpp:10.explain: Every call uses stack memory until it runs out.

cpp:10.prompt: Which data structure stores the pending recursive calls?
cpp:10.explain: Each call pushes a stack frame.

options: The recursive call is the last operation in the function
The recursive call is the first statement
cpp:10.explain: Nothing is left to do after the call returns.

options: The recursive call happens before the other work in the function
The call is the last operation
cpp:10.explain: Work happens while the calls return.

options: A function makes two or more recursive calls
Recursion on tree data structures only
A call passed as an argument
A function without a base case
cpp:10.explain: e.g. fib(n − 1) + fib(n − 2).

options: Function A calls B and B calls A
A function calls a library function
cpp:10.explain: The cycle goes through another function.

options: A recursive call is used as the argument of another recursive call
A recursive function defined inside another
A function calls itself within its own body
A calls B which calls A
A function is called from outside
cpp:10.explain: The simplest form of recursion.

options: Each call makes at most one recursive call
The recursion has no base case
cpp:10.explain: Like factorial: n × fact(n − 1).

cpp:10.prompt: Which technique avoids recomputing the same recursive calls (e.g. in Fibonacci)?
cpp:10.explain: Store results in a cache and reuse them.

cpp:10.prompt: How many calls does fact(5) make including the first call (base case n <= 1)?
cpp:10.explain: fact(5) → fact(4) → fact(3) → fact(2) → fact(1).

cpp:10.prompt: Any recursive algorithm can also be written…
options: iteratively using loops (and a stack if needed)
cpp:10.explain: Recursion and iteration are equally powerful.

options: Recursion that tries options and undoes a choice when it leads to a dead end
cpp:10.explain: Used for mazes, N-Queens, sudoku…

options: Split the problem into halves, solve each recursively, and combine
cpp:10.explain: Merge sort and binary search use it.

cpp:10.prompt: What typically happens in C++ when recursion is too deep?
options: The program crashes with a stack overflow (segmentation fault)
cpp:10.explain: There is no safety check; the stack simply overflows.

sql:1.prompt: Which DDL command creates a new database object such as a table, view or index?
sql:1.explain: `CREATE` creates a new database object such as a table, view or index.

sql:1.prompt: What does `CREATE` do?
options: Creates a new database object such as a table, view or index
Adds a description to a database object
Changes the name of a table or column
Changes the structure of an existing table

sql:1.prompt: Which DDL command changes the structure of an existing table?
sql:1.explain: `ALTER` changes the structure of an existing table.

sql:1.prompt: What does `ALTER` do?
options: Changes the structure of an existing table
Creates a new database object such as a table, view or index
Changes the name of a table or column
Deletes a table (structure and data) permanently
sql:1.explain: `ALTER` changes the structure of an existing table.

sql:1.prompt: Which DDL command deletes a table (structure and data) permanently?
sql:1.explain: `DROP` deletes a table (structure and data) permanently.

sql:1.prompt: What does `DROP` do?
options: Deletes a table (structure and data) permanently
Changes the name of a table or column
Creates a new database object such as a table, view or index
Adds a description to a database object
sql:1.explain: `DROP` deletes a table (structure and data) permanently.

sql:1.prompt: Which DDL command removes ALL rows quickly but keeps the table structure?
sql:1.explain: `TRUNCATE` removes ALL rows quickly but keeps the table structure.

sql:1.prompt: What does `TRUNCATE` do?
options: Removes ALL rows quickly but keeps the table structure
Changes the name of a table or column
Adds a description to a database object
Creates a new database object such as a table, view or index
sql:1.explain: `TRUNCATE` removes ALL rows quickly but keeps the table structure.

sql:1.prompt: Which DDL command changes the name of a table or column?

Changes the structure of an existing table

sql:1.prompt: Which DDL command adds a description to a database object?

sql:1.prompt: Which constraint uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL?
sql:1.explain: `PRIMARY KEY` uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL.

sql:1.prompt: What does `PRIMARY KEY` do?
options: Uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL
Links a column to the primary key of another table
Only allows values that satisfy a condition
Prevents duplicate values in a column
sql:1.explain: `PRIMARY KEY` uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL.

sql:1.prompt: Which constraint links a column to the primary key of another table?
sql:1.explain: `FOREIGN KEY` links a column to the primary key of another table.

sql:1.prompt: What does `FOREIGN KEY` do?
options: Links a column to the primary key of another table
Requires every row to have a value
Only allows values that satisfy a condition
Uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL
sql:1.explain: `FOREIGN KEY` links a column to the primary key of another table.

sql:1.prompt: Which constraint prevents duplicate values in a column?
sql:1.explain: `UNIQUE` prevents duplicate values in a column.

sql:1.prompt: What does `UNIQUE` do?
options: Prevents duplicate values in a column
Requires every row to have a value
Only allows values that satisfy a condition
Supplies a value when none is given
sql:1.explain: `UNIQUE` prevents duplicate values in a column.

sql:1.prompt: Which constraint requires every row to have a value?
sql:1.explain: `NOT NULL` requires every row to have a value.

sql:1.prompt: What does `NOT NULL` do?
options: Requires every row to have a value
Prevents duplicate values in a column
Only allows values that satisfy a condition
Supplies a value when none is given
sql:1.explain: `NOT NULL` requires every row to have a value.

sql:1.prompt: Which constraint only allows values that satisfy a condition?
sql:1.explain: `CHECK` only allows values that satisfy a condition.

sql:1.prompt: What does `CHECK` do?
options: Only allows values that satisfy a condition
Requires every row to have a value
Links a column to the primary key of another table
Prevents duplicate values in a column
sql:1.explain: `CHECK` only allows values that satisfy a condition.

sql:1.prompt: Which constraint supplies a value when none is given?
sql:1.explain: `DEFAULT` supplies a value when none is given.

sql:1.prompt: What does `DEFAULT` do?
options: Supplies a value when none is given
Requires every row to have a value
Prevents duplicate values in a column
Uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL
sql:1.explain: `DEFAULT` supplies a value when none is given.

sql:9.prompt: Which TCL command starts a transaction?
sql:9.explain: `BEGIN / START TRANSACTION` starts a transaction.

sql:9.prompt: What does `BEGIN / START TRANSACTION` do?
options: Marks a point inside a transaction
Undoes all changes since the transaction began
Undoes changes made after a savepoint
sql:9.explain: `BEGIN / START TRANSACTION` starts a transaction.

sql:9.prompt: Which TCL command saves all changes of the transaction permanently?
sql:9.explain: `COMMIT` saves all changes of the transaction permanently.

sql:9.prompt: What does `COMMIT` do?
options: Saves all changes of the transaction permanently
Undoes changes made after a savepoint
sql:9.explain: `COMMIT` saves all changes of the transaction permanently.

sql:9.prompt: Which TCL command undoes all changes since the transaction began?
sql:9.explain: `ROLLBACK` undoes all changes since the transaction began.

options: Undoes all changes since the transaction began
Sets properties such as the isolation level
Marks a point inside a transaction
sql:9.explain: `ROLLBACK` undoes all changes since the transaction began.

sql:9.prompt: Which TCL command marks a point inside a transaction?

Undoes changes made after a savepoint

Undoes all changes since the transaction began

sql:9.prompt: Which ACID property guarantees that a transaction can never leave a CHECK or FOREIGN KEY constraint violated?
sql:9.explain: Consistency.

sql:9.prompt: Which ACID property guarantees that two users running transactions at the same time do not see each other's unfinished changes?
sql:9.explain: Isolation.

sql:9.prompt: Which ACID property guarantees that a transfer that debits one account must also credit the other — or neither happens?
sql:9.explain: Atomicity.

sql:9.prompt: Which ACID property guarantees that after COMMIT, the data survives a power failure?
sql:9.explain: Durability.

sql:10.prompt: Which DCL keyword gives a user privileges on a database object?
sql:10.explain: `GRANT` gives a user privileges on a database object.

sql:10.prompt: What does `GRANT` do?
options: Gives a user privileges on a database object
Creates a named group of privileges
Refers to every privilege on an object
Takes privileges away from a user
sql:10.explain: `GRANT` gives a user privileges on a database object.

sql:10.prompt: Which privilege allows reading rows?
sql:10.explain: `SELECT` allows reading rows.

sql:10.prompt: What does `SELECT` do?
options: Allows creating a foreign key to the table
sql:10.explain: `SELECT` allows reading rows.

sql:10.prompt: What does DCL stand for?
sql:10.explain: GRANT and REVOKE.

sql:10.prompt: Fill the command that gives read access.
sql:10.code: ____ SELECT ON orders TO ravi;
sql:10.explain: GRANT … TO.

sql:10.prompt: Bug hunt! Which line causes an error?
sql:10.explain: REVOKE uses FROM, not TO.

sql:10.prompt: After these statements run (in order), which privileges does meera have on emp?
sql:10.explain: GRANT adds privileges, REVOKE removes them; ALL PRIVILEGES = every privilege. Work through the statements top to bottom.

sql:10.prompt: What does this statement do?
sql:10.code: REVOKE SELECT ON emp FROM nisha;
options: nisha can no longer read rows in emp
nisha can now read rows in emp
nisha can no longer add rows in emp
nisha is deleted from the database
sql:10.explain: GRANT gives privileges, REVOKE takes them away; WITH GRANT OPTION also lets the user grant the privilege to others.

sql:10.prompt: Which SQL sub-language does this statement belong to?
sql:10.code: ALTER TABLE emp RENAME TO emp_old;
sql:10.explain: DDL = structure (CREATE/ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE), DML = data changes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE), DQL = SELECT, DCL = permissions (GRANT/REVOKE), TCL = transactions (COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT).

sql:10.prompt: Which DCL keyword takes privileges away from a user?
sql:10.explain: `REVOKE` takes privileges away from a user.

sql:10.prompt: What does `REVOKE` do?
options: Takes privileges away from a user
Refers to every privilege on an object
Lets the receiver grant the same privilege to others
Creates a named group of privileges
sql:10.explain: `REVOKE` takes privileges away from a user.

sql:10.prompt: Which privilege allows adding rows?
sql:10.explain: `INSERT` allows adding rows.

sql:10.prompt: What does `INSERT` do?
options: Allows creating a foreign key to the table
sql:10.explain: `INSERT` allows adding rows.

sql:10.prompt: Which keyword follows the user name in REVOKE?
sql:10.explain: GRANT … TO, REVOKE … FROM.

sql:10.prompt: Fill the keyword.
sql:10.code: REVOKE DELETE ON orders ____ ravi;
sql:10.explain: REVOKE … FROM.

sql:10.prompt: After these statements run (in order), which privileges does kiran have on invoices?
sql:10.explain: GRANT adds privileges, REVOKE removes them; ALL PRIVILEGES = every privilege. Work through the statements top to bottom.

sql:10.prompt: What does this statement do?

rohan can now read rows in emp
rohan can now add rows in emp
